files.role: Public in-memory primitives and a private dense-counts byte codec for stable-partition row mapping: CountsMatrix, streaming builder, prefix rank, point translation and sweep translation. Labels are destination-list indices, not fragment IDs. Production label-column IO/cache ownership is outside this module. Private state prevents ordinary direct mutation but decode deliberately separates structural decoding from semantic count validation.
files.limits: All 697 lines and local tests were inspected; none were executed. The comments locate label IO/cache responsibilities in lance-index, whose implementation remains pending. Do not infer a released stable file-format contract or dataset-version gate from this helper's local codec version1. Full FRI schema/reader selection and whether callers always call validate are unknown. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:4-60; rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:74-82; rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:191-290) Local tests omit wrong-version decoding, excess live-row budgets, maximum destination count/overflow, short validity buffers and empty/excess-input sweeps. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:484-697)
ranges: License and design for reordered rewrites: one nullable u16 destination label per old physical row in caller scan order; NULL means deleted. Rows may interleave among destinations but each destination must preserve relative source order. Parallel writers must merge their output in that order. Arbitrary within-destination permutations cannot be represented by these labels alone and require explicit final offsets in another format. This is a correctness precondition rather than a runtime test here.

Cumulative counts are stored per destination at each fixed-size block end. Point translation combines count before the block with within-block exclusive prefix rank; a sequential sweep seeds all counters at a block boundary and increments by label. The block is also the documented label IO/cache unit, but that IO belongs to lance-index and is not implemented here. Approximate dense-grid footprint examples omit header/Vec overhead; exact payload size is ceil(total_rows/block_rows)*num_destinations*4. Imports supply core DeepSizeOf/Error/Result and Arrow NullBuffer.

Public defaults: DEFAULT_BLOCK_ROWS=64*1024 (65536), MAX_DESTINATIONS=u16::MAX+1 (65536). Private codec constants: magic LSPC, version1, fixed28-byte header, representation0 for dense little-endian u32 grid; unknown future tags are rejected. corrupt wraps messages as CorruptFile named stable_partition_counts. These local codec constants are not proof of a Lance dataset format version or released stability designation.

Public CountsMatrix derives Clone/Debug/PartialEq/Eq with private destination count, block rows, total old physical rows u64 (including deleted), and row-major cumulative Vec<u32>. Each matrix row is through the end of a block, unlike the exclusive count-before accessor. Deleted counts are implicit differences from physical row budgets.

Accessors return stored dimensions; num_blocks divides cumulative cell count by destination count, relying on construction/decode shape checks. block_of divides an arbitrary row by block_rows and casts to usize without range validation. block_range computes start=block*block_rows and end=min(start+block_rows,total_rows), with ordinary arithmetic and no bounds check: an invalid block can yield start>end or overflow. Private block_row slices the flattened grid and panics if its indices are invalid.

count_before(block,label) returns0 for block0 without label validation, otherwise indexes the preceding matrix row. counters_at_block similarly returns a newly allocated zero vector for block0 or clones the previous row. Both permit the end boundary block==num_blocks on a valid matrix; they do not return Result and callers own bounds validation.

total(label) returns0 for an empty matrix without checking the label, otherwise indexes the last row. total_live_rows sums that final row as u64 or returns0. deleted_through(block) subtracts the current cumulative live sum from the block end; it assumes valid monotonic/budget counts and a valid block. Using malformed decoded counts before validate can underflow ordinary arithmetic.

validate iterates all blocks, rejects any label count that decreases from the previous block, and rejects the increase in total live rows if it exceeds the current physical block length. It returns contextual CorruptFile through corrupt; O(blocks*destinations) scanning is why decode does not do this automatically. Private shape invariants ensure complete matrix rows; validation does not compare counts against the actual label column or destination fragment metadata.

encode reserves header+cells*4 bytes and writes LSPC, version1, repr0, destination count, block_rows as little-endian u32, total_rows as little-endian u64, then every cumulative u32 in row-major order. Header offsets are0,4,8,12,16,20; payload begins28. It does not call validate or return Result; capacity arithmetic is unchecked in source.

decode first requires28 bytes, rejects wrong magic, unsupported version and representation tags other than0 via CorruptFile. Version and representation fields use exact byte slices after the header length check, so their array conversions are structurally guarded. Dimension/row-count extraction follows at rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:264-266.

decode extracts destination count, block rows and total rows from little-endian header fields, then calls check_shape before division; invalid destination count or zero block rows yields InvalidInput, despite being read from persisted bytes. It computes ceil(total_rows/block_rows), checks block-count*destinations*4 for overflow and exact equality with remaining bytes, rejecting truncation and trailing bytes as CorruptFile. It reserves/reads the grid as u32 little-endian chunks and returns without validate. Structural success alone does not prove monotonic counts or per-block row budgets.

Private check_shape accepts destination counts1..=65536 and any positive block_rows; it returns descriptive InvalidInput otherwise. check_label compares a u16 label as u32 against destination count and also returns InvalidInput. The maximum valid label is65535; the default block size is advisory, not enforced.

CountsMatrix DeepSizeOf reports cumulative Vec capacity times sizeof(u32), excluding inline storage already accounted by the trait convention. Public CountsMatrixBuilder derives Debug with private shape, per-destination running u32 counters, cumulative cells, total physical-row count and rows-in-current-block. No shared mutable/concurrent state is exposed.

try_new validates shape, allocates zeroed running counters for each destination, initializes cumulative empty and both physical-row counters zero. Empty input is valid and will produce zero matrix rows at finish.

push accepts one Option<u16> per old physical row. For Some, reject out-of-range label and checked per-destination u32 increment overflow before advancing any physical counters; None only advances physical counters. total_rows increments as ordinary u64. When rows_in_block reaches block_rows, append a full snapshot of all running counters and reset rows_in_block to zero. A destination can hold at most u32::MAX rows, whose last zero-based offset is u32::MAX-1; this builder cannot represent count2^32.

finish consumes the builder, appends one final cumulative row only when the last block is partial, and moves cumulative/shape/total fields into CountsMatrix. Exact block multiples get no extra row; empty input keeps zero rows. No secondary validation pass occurs.

Public rank_label_prefix counts matching label values strictly before upto, ignoring positions invalid in NullBuffer. If validity is absent or reports no nulls, it skips per-element validity checks. Slicing values[..upto] enforces bounds by panic, not Result; no validity-length check exists, and counts cast usize to u32. In intended blocks limited to u32 rows the count fits; an arbitrary standalone oversized slice could truncate. Work is linear in prefix length with no output allocation.

translate_in_block first derives block length via block_range, then returns InvalidInput if values length differs or position is outside it. It does not separately validate the block index before block_range arithmetic. A supplied validity buffer is not length-checked. These checks establish the requested values slice size and position, not consistency of counts and labels.

For an invalid/NULL position return Ok(None) before reading or validating the underlying label, so arbitrary null payload values are allowed. Otherwise validate that label, compute count_before(block,label)+rank_label_prefix(values,validity,pos,label) using ordinary u32 addition, and return (label,offset). There is no destination-fragment-ID lookup, comparison with final destination totals, or validation that every supplied prefix label matches the stored counts.

Public SweepTranslator derives Debug and privately owns a Vec<u32> of per-destination counters. new rejects start_block >= max(num_blocks,1), allowing block0 for an empty matrix but not the end boundary for a nonempty matrix. It seeds counters from CountsMatrix::counters_at_block; only a block boundary is expressible.

advance(None) returns None and changes no counter. Some(label) checks counter-vector bounds, returns the old counter as offset and increments with ordinary u32 addition, unlike the builder's checked increment. It tracks neither processed physical rows nor remaining dataset length: an empty or exhausted sweep can accept further valid labels. Caller must feed the correct ordered row stream and avoid overflow; no matrix consistency validation happens here.

Tests use seeded StdRng and Rng/SeedableRng traits and NullBuffer. random_labels makes a NULL with probability1/8, otherwise a uniform destination label. build uses the public builder and unwraps each valid fixture operation. These helpers are local; runtime tests were not executed during KB analysis.

reference independently assigns monotonically increasing offsets per label using HashMap counters, preserving NULL positions. block_slices turns optional labels into a values vector with 0xBEEF garbage at NULL positions and creates a validity buffer only if any null exists. This explicitly tests null payload exclusion instead of relying on zero fill.

Hand example uses labels[0,2,NULL,2,1,1,0,2,NULL,0], three destinations and blocks of four. It validates the matrix, expects three blocks for ten physical rows and range8..10 for the last, and checks exclusive count-before values including the legal block3 end boundary.

The same fixture asserts destination totals3/2/3, total live8, deleted-through prefixes1 then2 and counters at block1=[1,0,2]. Exact first-eight-row input produces two blocks; empty input has zero blocks/rows/live/label totals and validates. These tests distinguish partial-final, exact-multiple and empty layouts.

Round trip uses seed7,1000 rows,five destinations,block64 and compares decoded equality before validate; empty also round-trips. Short bytes, corrupt magic, a one-byte truncation and repr9 fail decoding. A manually decreased cumulative cell is encoded and decoded successfully, then fails validate, demonstrating the intentional separation. Test assertions mostly check is_err, not exact categories/messages.

Builder rejects zero destinations, destination count aboveMAX_DESTINATIONS, zero block size and out-of-range label3 for m3; valid label2 then succeeds. The test does not assert exact error variants/messages, state after failed push or u32 counter overflow.

Seed42 fixture has1000 rows,five destinations,block64. Every point translation across every block is compared with the independent per-label reference using garbage null payloads; sweeps beginning at every valid block boundary are compared over the entire remaining label stream. This verifies point/sweep order agreement on one seeded mixed-null input, not arbitrary within-destination permutation support.

Input checks use one four-row block and assert errors for wrong values length, out-of-range position, live label9 for m2, invalid sweep block1 and advance label9. Although a comment calls an out-of-range data label corruption, check_label actually returns InvalidInput (rust/lance-core/src/utils/stable_partition.rs:306-314). Short validity buffers, overflow and extra sweep input are not tested here; module ends.

files.role: Public MappingReader contract and OrderedCompactionMapping adapter for one rewrite group. Graph traversal and index/manifest orchestration are explicitly outside this file.
ranges: SPDX and module docs place graph traversal in the FRI reader. Imports bring shared Arc ownership, async_trait expansion, RowAddrRemap, core deep-size context/trait and Error/Result. FRI expansion and RowAddrRemap algorithm are not defined by these imports.

Public async-trait MappingReader requires Send+Sync+Debug+DeepSizeOf. Despite row_id names, the contract explicitly says physical addresses. remap_row_id(&self,u64)->Result<Option<u64>> returns mapped address or None for deleted source row; addresses outside source fragments or outside their valid offset ranges must return InvalidInput. Persisted invalid mappings should produce CorruptFile and storage errors propagate. These error requirements are an interface contract; the trait cannot enforce every implementation.

Default remap_row_ids(&self,&[u64])->Result<Vec<Option<u64>>> reserves input length, iterates in input order and sequentially awaits remap_row_id, pushing one result per input. Duplicates and None positions are preserved, empty input gives empty Vec, and the first Err stops iteration and discards the partial result. There is no concurrent buffering or aggregation. Cancellation can interrupt an in-flight single-row future; the trait makes no rollback promise for implementation side effects.

OrderedCompactionMapping derives Debug and privately owns Arc<RowAddrRemap>. Documentation calls it an adapter for one group's existing bitmap/rank remap, explicitly not replacing the legacy FRI reader or writer. Public new simply stores the Arc; its documentation presumes fragment layout validation happened when the remap was constructed, and no additional validation is performed here.

Private map_row_id invokes remap.get(row_id).ok_or_else with an InvalidInput message containing the full u64 row ID when the outer Option is absent. Present inner None passes through as deleted; present Some(address) passes through as mapped. DeepSizeOf delegates to the Arc remap children with the same Context, inheriting Arc dedup (rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:182-190). The remap's local memory calculation and layout validation are now analyzed at rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:167-174, rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:391-470 and rust/lance-core/src/utils/row_addr_remap.rs:563-625; persisted IO and caller integration remain pending.

The async-trait implementation overrides both operations. Single maps synchronously through map_row_id; batch maps the borrowed slice through that helper and collects Result<Vec<Option<u64>>>. It avoids per-item async awaits and preserves order/duplicates; collect short-circuits on the first error. There is no internal await/yield or IO in these adapter bodies, though the interface is async.

Private cfg(test) imports RowAddress, GroupInputWithLayout and RoaringTreemap. Unit SingleRowReader derives Debug/DeepSizeOf and implements only single-row mapping: u64::MAX returns InvalidInput, zero gives None, others echo Some(row_id). It therefore exercises the trait default batch implementation rather than the adapter override.

Tokio test default_batch_preserves_positions_and_propagates_errors expects [2,0,1,2] -> [Some(2),None,Some(1),Some(2)], checks empty input, then [1,u64::MAX] produces InvalidInput with the precise test-message substring. It checks error category/text, not cancellation or post-error side effects.

The ordered-compaction test constructs a real RowAddrRemap through compact_with_layout: source fragments (1,3 rows),(2,1 row), surviving addresses (1,0),(1,2),(2,0), destination fragments (3,2 rows),(4,1 row). Its input is (2,0),(1,1),(1,0),(1,0), covering out-of-source-order requests, deletion and duplicate. Expected results are computed from remap.get and both batch and singles must equal them. This is an adapter-equivalence test, not an independent expected-address oracle for the underlying remap algorithm.

The same test checks empty batch and both absent fragment (99,0) and out-of-range offset (1,3). Each must error through single and batch calls with InvalidInput and message containing outside compaction mapping. No CorruptFile/storage-error path is exercised by this adapter fixture. Tests were read, not run.

The adapter's RowAddrRemap dependency and how callers select mapping chains remain pending; do not use this file alone to claim full compaction or stable-ID semantics. files.role: Public deep-memory-estimation trait and pointer-deduplication context, derive-macro re-export, standard-library/Arrow implementations, private recursive Arrow-buffer accounting, and local tests.
ranges: SPDX lines, public re-export of lance_derive::DeepSizeOf in the macro namespace, and imports for size_of/size_of_val, collections, atomics, Arc/locks, Arrow arrays/buffers/data. The same DeepSizeOf spelling is also used for the trait below; derive expansion implementation is in another crate and remains pending.

Context is a public struct with a private HashSet<usize> of seen identities. Default calls new; new starts empty. mark_seen(ptr) directly returns set insertion success, true only for a newly inserted integer. The caller supplies pointer identity and a mutable context; there is no reset API or synchronization layer. The context tracking set itself is not charged by these formulas.

DeepSizeOf is public. Its default deep_size_of adds size_of_val(self) to deep_size_of_children with a fresh Context; the latter is required and receives mutable traversal state. Separate top-level calls cannot deduplicate against each other. Implementations must count descendant heap storage without recounting their own inline footprint and should propagate the same context when deduplication is intended.

Private impl_deep_size_primitive macro emits trait implementations returning zero children. The invocation covers u8/u16/u32/u64/u128/usize, i8/i16/i32/i64/i128/isize, f32/f64, bool and (). This list excludes char and other numeric wrappers; their support is not implied by the macro. Their inline size still comes from the default method.

str reports zero child storage because its dynamically sized bytes are its own size_of_val; String reports capacity, not current length, as heap children. Thus direct str and owned String accounting use different ownership boundaries.

bytes::Bytes uses as_ptr as a usize key. On first sight it charges self.len(), otherwise zero. This is exact start-pointer deduplication, not underlying-allocation identity or capacity accounting: distinct offsets can be counted separately and equal-start views of different lengths are sensitive to visitation order. These limitations follow from the key/formula; external Bytes allocation details are not reviewed here.

AtomicU64 and AtomicUsize both return zero children without loading their stored numeric value. The top-level default counts their inline representation. No other atomic type implementation is present in this range.

Fixed [T;N] and dynamically sized [T] sum only element child sizes using the same context; inline elements are already counted by the owner or size_of_val. Slice comments explicitly identify Box<[T]> and Arc<[T]> as owners that count slice bytes; adding those bytes again in the slice implementation would double-count them.

RwLock<T> obtains a read guard and Mutex<T> an exclusive guard, then delegates to protected T children. A poisoned-lock Err returns zero, silently undercounting children. These are blocking lock acquisitions with no timeout and no Result returned; memory estimation can wait on contention or deadlock under an incompatible already-held lock. The lock wrapper inline footprint comes from its owner/default method.

Private impl_deep_size_tuple macro emits generic implementations requiring every tuple component DeepSizeOf, destructures self under allow(non_snake_case), and sums each component children. Invocations cover tuple arities two through six only. The tuple inline layout/padding is counted by its owning object/default method, not by this sum.

Vec<T> charges capacity*size_of::<T>() plus children of live elements only. Uninitialized spare capacity contributes bytes but is not traversed. The Vec header is counted at the enclosing inline boundary. Arithmetic is ordinary usize multiplication/addition, with no overflow handling.

Box<T:?Sized> always charges pointee size_of_val plus pointee children. Arc<T:?Sized> first casts its data pointer through *const () to usize (discarding metadata), deduplicates it, and only on first sight charges pointee size plus children. Arc control-block/refcount and allocator overhead are not explicitly counted. Marking before recursive descent permits repeated Arc identities to be skipped; this is not general graph-cycle detection for arbitrary custom implementations.
Option<T> delegates to Some inner children or returns zero for None. The discriminant and inline T storage are left to the parent/default footprint rather than counted again.

HashMap<K,V,S> supports any hasher type parameter and estimates backing storage as capacity*(size_of::<K>()+size_of::<V>()+1), then adds live key/value children. The comment calls the one-byte term approximate control metadata and notes capacity/buckets; the code uses reported capacity directly. Alignment, allocator overhead and exact table layout are not measured, so this is an estimate.

HashSet<K> (default hasher form) estimates capacity*(size_of::<K>()+1) plus live key children. It does not define the generic-S HashSet implementation analogous to HashMap. The one-byte overhead is approximate.

BTreeMap estimates len*(size_of::<K>()+size_of::<V>()+3*size_of::<usize>()) plus live key/value children. BTreeSet uses len*(size_of::<K>()+3*size_of::<usize>()) plus live key children. Comments motivate roughly three pointer words per entry based on an average B-tree node. These formulas do not inspect actual node count, node occupancy or allocations.

Private record_array_data walks every data buffer, adding its capacity if its as_ptr integer is first seen; it similarly accounts for the null bit-buffer obtained through inner().inner(), then recursively visits child_data. The shared Context deduplicates identical start addresses across descendants. No explicit ArrayData metadata or child-vector allocation charge is added.

The dyn Array implementation calls to_data and delegates to record_array_data. The comment describes to_data as cloning Arcs rather than data bytes and says this creates a small O(number of buffers) metadata cost; that is the source comment, not an independently verified property of every dependency Array implementation. The returned estimate accounts for the traversed buffers.

RecordBatch sums deep_size_of_children for each column Arc with one context. It has no explicit charge here for its column-vector allocation or schema metadata. Default deep_size_of separately counts the inline RecordBatch. Sharing the same Array Arc across columns is deduplicated by Arc accounting before buffer traversal.

ScalarBuffer<T> is implemented where T:ArrowNativeType. It obtains the inner Buffer, deduplicates as_ptr, and charges capacity only once. The comment chooses capacity rather than slice length because sliced buffers retain backing storage; the implementation key is still a start pointer, not an owning-allocation identifier. Changed start pointers can therefore defeat same-key deduplication.

The cfg(test) module imports Arrow fixtures and the local trait/context. test_basic_record_batch makes one Int32 column [1,2,3] and asserts deep size >=12 bytes. It verifies a lower bound, not exact RecordBatch metadata accounting.

test_same_batch_dedup uses one Context for repeated RecordBatch child-size calls; first must be positive, second exactly zero. The test deliberately avoids fresh-context deep_size_of, demonstrating traversal-local deduplication.
test_arc_dedup clones an Arc<RecordBatch>, then measures both with the same Context and requires first positive, second zero. This exercises shared batch identity before child traversal.

test_multi_column_shared_array places two clones of the same Int32 Array Arc in a two-column batch and compares its child estimate with a one-column batch measured using a separate Context. Equality proves the tested shared-array case is counted once; it does not prove equality of complete allocated batch sizes.

test_nested_struct_array constructs Int32 and String children under one StructArray in a RecordBatch. It requires deep size >12, a weak traversal lower bound rather than an exact byte total or proof of every child-buffer contribution.

test_std_types checks exact inline u32 size, String >=header+5, Vec<u32> >=header+three u32 element sizes, and Arc<u32> children four then zero in one Context. Lower-bound assertions permit extra capacity/overhead; the Arc test isolates identity deduplication.

test_derive_macro imports the derive macro, defines local Outer {count:u64,label:String,inner:Inner} and Inner {values:Vec<u32>} with derives, then requires size >=size_of::<Outer>()+5+12 for the constructed fixture. It tests macro usability/recursive heap accounting at a lower bound, not the macro implementation itself. No local cases validate Bytes aliases, scalar-buffer offset aliases, poisoned locks or collection-estimate accuracy. Tests were read, not executed.
